title: Scope private-beta signing secrets to the build step
summary: Separate unprivileged private-beta validation from protected signing and expose signing credentials only to the exact certificate-import and Tauri build step.
reason: Remediate AUDIT-FIND-W10-014, which exposes updater and Windows signing credentials to every job step, including dependency installation and repository tests.
behavior_before: Updater and Authenticode signing secrets were declared at job scope and therefore readable by checkout/setup actions, dependency lifecycle scripts, tests, and unrelated release steps.
behavior_after: An unprivileged job validates and emits a SHA-256-bound nonsecret handoff; the protected signing job verifies it before one step-local secret scope imports the certificate, builds signed artifacts, and removes the certificate.
tests_added: Workflow policy parsing proves unsigned validation and protected signing are separate jobs with least-privilege permissions and no validation-job secret references.
Sentinel signing credentials resolve only in the reviewed consuming step; the public updater key resolves only in preflight and build.
Dependency installation and SHA-256 handoff verification precede the sole private-secret step.
Certificate-store and temporary PFX cleanup are inside finally and fail closed when credential artifacts remain.
Preflight can defer private-secret presence while still generating and validating nonsecret updater configuration.
manual_validation: Workflow YAML parsing, GitHub audit-spine hardening, touched Python Ruff/compileall, and 53 private-beta tooling tests passed; the focused secret-scope/preflight selection passed 11 tests.
Risky-file registry, test-subsystem inventory, architecture, naming, and god-file checks passed; god-file output contained warnings only.

A full Windows release build with -Zip -Verify -IncludeTests copied 18,439 files and ran for 983 seconds. Package policy, environment, Tauri prerequisites, tool integration, and end-to-end smoke passed; aggregate verification exited 1 only on established WebView static-asset, dependency-cycle, generated/status-document, tracked-office-document, and unrelated Ruff baselines.

A fresh exact release-policy copy matched all six included implementation/test/document paths by SHA-256 and passed four package-applicable tests with seven expected skips because .github workflow metadata is intentionally excluded from release packages.

Not run: protected GitHub Actions execution with disposable updater/private certificate credentials, successful signed NSIS/updater artifact production, and post-signature verification. This external acceptance prerequisite keeps the packet in_progress.
rollback_plan: Revert the split-job workflow, nonsecret handoff verification, scoped preflight option, secret-scope policy tests, documentation, generated artifacts, and packet metadata together. Do not restore job-level signing-secret declarations.
notes: High-risk release-secret boundary. Local implementation and nonsecret validation are complete, but the audit's Rung 6 acceptance requires a protected GitHub environment run with disposable signing credentials and verified signed artifacts; that external prerequisite is unavailable here, so status remains in_progress. No signing credential was loaded, and no remote workflow dispatch, release publication, signing, GitHub mutation, lifecycle action, or media access occurred. Existing overlapping batch-020 and batch-037 edits in the workflow, preflight, tests, checker, and private-beta documentation were preserved. Known unrelated worktree baselines remain outside this packet: stale generated summaries, DOC005 at the active audit BASELINE reference, the mediapipeline.core.processes to mediapipeline.core.queue dependency cycle, two rename-test Ruff B023 findings, the WebView static-asset reliability assertion, tracked-office-document findings, and generated/status-document drift. Immutable audit evidence remained read-only.
